interactions.summary: Students propose that the frozen lake figures endless revenge, abandoned free will, and betrayal as a force that freezes relationship itself.
Jiang confirms that treachery traps souls in the instant of betrayal, cancels free movement, and is worst because it freezes the universe's imaginative motion in place.
A student reads the Ugolino passage and Jiang asks what exactly in the story disturbs Dante and creates interpretive difficulty.

claims.claim: Jiang says the frozen lake represents souls immobilized in the exact moment of betrayal and revenge, unable to move beyond that instant.
Jiang argues that the damned in the deepest hell have lost the imaginative and loving capacity required for free will.
Jiang says betrayal is punished most severely because the universe is ordered by motion and treachery freezes that living motion in place.

signature_moments.moment: Hell's bottom is a soul jammed forever into the instant when betrayal happened.
signature_moments.source_phrase: he's just stuck in that moment
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns punishment into a metaphysics of arrested time rather than a merely physical torture scene.

signature_moments.moment: Treachery is worst because it freezes the universe itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: betrayal treachery freezes the universe in place
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's compact causal account of why imaginative corruption outranks many other sins.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's image for the deepest hell as treachery turned into literal and metaphysical immobility.
The sin that freezes the universe's imaginative movement and traps souls in revenge.

chronology_notes.note: This packet consolidates the lecture's running theme that hell's structure measures damage to imagination and free movement, now applied specifically to treachery.
